facts.text: ISO 16001 sets performance requirements and tests for object detection and operator visibility aids on earth-moving machines, while ISO 5006 defines how the operator's own field of view is measured.
facts.quote: ISO 16001 sets performance requirements and tests for the systems that detect objects and help the operator see around an earth-moving machine, and ISO 5006 defines how the operator's own field of view is measured.

facts.text: ISO 16001:2017 is edition 2, confirmed in 2023; its regional versions include EN ISO 16001:2017 in Europe and AS ISO 16001:2020 in Australia.
facts.quote: ISO 16001:2017 (edition 2, confirmed 2023; also EN ISO 16001:2017 in Europe and AS ISO 16001:2020 in Australia)

facts.text: The booklet found ISO 16001 to be the only off-road standard with hard detection and warning numbers and the only per-technology test annexes.
facts.quote: ISO 16001 supplies the only hard off-road numbers for detection latency and warnings and the only per-technology test annexes

facts.text: ISO 16001 covers object detection systems (ODS) and visibility aids such as cameras and mirrors on ISO 6165 machines; its scope concerns warning, not braking.
facts.quote: It covers object detection systems (ODS) and visibility aids such as cameras and mirrors on ISO 6165 machines. It is about warning, not braking.

facts.text: ISO 16001 requires detection time to be no more than 300 ms.
facts.quote: detection time not more than 300 ms

facts.text: ISO 16001 requires unambiguous detection with an uninterrupted sequence of the signal.
facts.quote: detection "unambiguously with an uninterrupted sequence of the signal"

facts.text: ISO 16001 requires an audible warning at least 3 dB above ambient noise, preferably at 500 to 3,400 Hz.
facts.quote: an audible warning at least 3 dB above ambient noise, preferably at 500 to 3,400 Hz

facts.text: ISO 16001 specifies a flashing red light within a 120 degree arc as the most severe visual warning.
facts.quote: a flashing red light within a 120 degree arc as the most severe visual warning

facts.text: ISO 16001 does not permit warnings by vibration alone.
ISO 16001 requires self-check at start-up and continuous fault monitoring.
facts.quote: self-check at start-up and continuous fault monitoring

facts.text: ISO 16001 permits deactivation only by two or more separate and distinct actions.
facts.quote: deactivation only by "two or more separate and distinct actions"

facts.text: ISO 16001 requires electromagnetic compatibility to ISO 13766.
ISO 16001 says false signals from fog, snow, rain, wind and dust should be minimized, but supplies no numerical criterion for that recommendation.
facts.quote: False signals from fog, snow, rain, wind and dust "should be minimized", a "should" with no number

facts.text: ISO 16001 uses a test body consisting of a person or a standard measuring unit representative of a person, sized in technology annexes for CCTV, radar, ultrasonic, transponder, electromagnetic transceiver, surround view and vision systems.
facts.quote: The test body is "a person or a standard measuring unit representative of a person", sized in technology annexes for CCTV, radar, ultrasonic, transponder, electromagnetic transceiver, surround view and vision systems

facts.text: ISO 16001's detection zone test is a physical test on the machine or a representative configuration.
facts.quote: the detection zone test is a physical test on the machine or a representative configuration

facts.text: The booklet lists ISO 5006, the standard for measuring the operator's field of view from the cab and mapping blind areas, as not verified.
facts.quote: ISO 5006 is the standard for measuring the operator's field of view from the cab and mapping blind areas. The booklet lists it as not verified [Chapter 3]

facts.text: The booklet proposes reproducing ISO 5006 and ISO 16001 visibility-type methods and the small-cylinder method of UN R159 in a digital twin of each machine to compute coverage and blind zones before hardware arrives.
facts.quote: ISO 5006 and ISO 16001 visibility-type methods, with the small-cylinder method of UN R159, as the geometric approach that a digital twin of each machine can reproduce to compute coverage and blind zones before hardware arrives

facts.text: The booklet's plan runs ISO 16001 annex tests for each candidate sensor technology.
facts.quote: the booklet's plan runs its annex tests for each candidate sensor technology [Chapter 3]

facts.text: ISO 16001 has no lidar annex, no quantified weather conditions and no false-alarm rate; the booklet concludes that the manufacturer must argue the evidence for these gaps.
facts.quote: no lidar annex, no quantified weather conditions and no false-alarm rate, so that evidence must be argued by the manufacturer [Chapter 3]
